title: Bar chart
summary: A bar chart: values by category as columns or bars, grouped or stacked (also as shares), with a value axis from zero, a legend that hides series, a tooltip, a keyboard cursor, a summary in words and the same data as a table.

template.description: Template variant name for SfBaseElement external templates.

label.description: What the chart shows, in a few words: its accessible name, the table's caption and the file name of an export. Required in practice: without it the chart is named «Диаграмма».

x.description: The field of the categories; the first field when unset.

y.description: The field of the values, or a comma list of fields, one series per field (the wide form); every numeric field when unset.

series.description: The long form: one series per distinct value of this field, the values from the first y field.

x-scale.description: auto reads the categories: dates stand in time order and read as dates, anything else stays in the order given. A bar chart's axis is always bands.

y-max.description: The end of the value axis; the data's own when unset. Ignored by normalized.

stack.description: none: the series' bars stand side by side in each category; stacked: on one another, positive up and negative down from zero; normalized: each stack as shares of its whole, 0–100 %.

orientation.description: vertical: columns over categories along the bottom; horizontal: bars from the left, categories down the side, for long names and rankings.

sort.description: The order of the categories: as given, or by their total, smallest or largest first.

value-labels.description: end: each bar's value (a stack's total) at its end, where it fits; never in normalized.

legend.description: auto shows the legend above the plot when there are two series or more. Each entry is a button that hides and shows its series.

tooltip.description: axis: under the pointer or the cursor, every series' value in that category; in normalized, its share and its value.

grid.description: value: guide lines across the plot at the value ticks; none: only the zero line.

x-label.description: The name of the categories, under a vertical chart; it heads the table's first column (the x field's own name when unset).

y-label.description: The name of the values, above a vertical chart and under a horizontal one.

x-format.description: For dates as categories: auto, or an Intl date style (short, medium, long, full).

y-format.description: number, integer, decimal-<n>, percent (a share 0..1), compact or currency-<CODE>, in the page's language.

size.description: The rung of the size ladder: the plot's height, the text and the gaps. 1/2 for a card, 2 for a page of its own.

table.description: The same data as a table: toggle offers a button that swaps the plot for it, visible shows it under the plot, hidden keeps it for screen readers only. Never none: the table is the chart's text.

summary.description: auto: a sentence of the data (how many categories, each series' highest and lowest), said before the plot and kept for screen readers. The description slot adds the host's own words.

data-state.description: auto: ready with data, empty without. loading draws the frame without bars; error offers «Повторить», which sends refresh.

items.description: The data: a list of records ([{city, sales}, …]) or an object of columns. One bar per category and series. A missing value (null, '', a word) is a gap: no bar, never a zero.

names.description: What each series is called, by its key: {sales: «Продажи»}. A series without a name is called by its key.

hidden-series.description: The keys of the series the person hid with the legend.

reset.summary: Shows every series again and takes the cursor away.

sf-bar-chart-toggle.summary: The person hid or showed a series with its legend button; applied at once (the vocabulary's local toggle).

sf-bar-chart-select.summary: The person chose a bar: a click on the plot, or Enter or Space on the keyboard cursor.

sf-bar-chart-refresh.summary: The person asked for the data again from the error state; the host loads it and sets items.

accessibility.focus: One Tab stop on the plot, then the legend buttons and the table button. The summary is the plot's description; each cursor move is said politely.

ai_guidance.use_when: Use sf-bar-chart to compare values across categories, or the parts of each category's whole (stack).
do_not: Do not draw a chart without a label
Do not replace missing values with zero
Do not use it for a long series over time; that is sf-line-chart
